txt: FATEJ, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 35 m. NW of Koursk, district and 32 m. E of Dmitriev, on a height near the r. bank of the Ousoja. Pop. 1,900.
FATIANAVO, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Pskov, 35 m. ESE of Ostrov.

FELLIN, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Livonia, district and 40 m. ESE of Pernau, and 123 m. NE of Riga, on the N bank of Lake Virtz- Ervé, near the egress of a small river of the same name, an affluent of the Navast. Pop. 658. It is ill-built, and has no edifice except a church worthy of notice. The origin of this town dates from a very early period. In 1224 it was fortified by the Livonians, and several times successfully resisted the attacks of the Russians. It was taken in 1482 and 1560 by the czar Ivan-Vasiliévitch, and reduced to ashes; and subsequently passed into the hands of the Poles and Swedes.
FELSTIN, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Podolia, district and 14 m. SW of Proskourov, and 48 m. N of Kamenetz. Pop. 680. $

txt: FILINSKOE', a parish and village of Russia in Asia, in the gov. and 135 m. NNE of Tobolsk, on the r. bank of the Irtish. FILIOS, FILBAS, or FILIYAS, a river of Turkey in Asia, in the sanj. of Boli, formed by the union of the Buiuk-su and Kutchuk-su, the first of which descends from the Cheleh-dagh, and the second from the Hermarouz-dagh, and which unite near Boli. Thence the united stream runs N, and, after a total course of about 75 m., falls into the Black sea, a little to the E of a village of the same name. Its principal affluent is the Ova, which it receives on the r. This river is the Billœus of the ancients.
FILIPOVSKAIA, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of the Don Cossacks, 6 m. SW of Goughiuskaïa, and 126 m. ENE of Novo-Tcherkask, near the r. bank of the Don.

FINLAND, a government or administrative division of Russia, lying between the parallels of 60° and 70° N, and between 21° and 32° E long. On the N it is bounded by Lapland; on the E by the Russian govs. of Archangel and Olonetz; on the S by the gov. of Petersburg and the gulf of Finland; and on the W by Sweden and the gulf of Bothnia. Besides the former Swedish province of the same name, it comprehends all the gov. of Viburg, or the ancient Russian Finland. It stretches to the highest north; and comprehends a territorial surface of 144,000 sq. m., with a pop. of 1,400,000, which is said to be rapidly increasing. On the N and W some branches of the Scandinavian mountains enter this gov.; on the E it is covered with sand-hills and rocks, and intersected by marshes, seas, lakes, and rivers, which diffuse cold and unwholesome mists. The most central lake in the country—the Payana, or 'the Peaceable'—is about 72 m. in length, and 13 m. in breadth. The lake of Saima on the E, which is crowded with islands, is still larger; and discharges its superfluent waters in a series of six cataracts to the Tornea, which carries its waters into the Ladoga lake. The coasts of the Bothnian and Finland gulfs are thickly strewn with granite and limestone rocks, and in some places present a labyrinthine archipelago of little islands. …
FITTAH, the cap. of the Russian prov. of Shirvan. It became the cap, of the prov. in the early part of the present century, when Shamekhia was laid in ruins. Pop. 28,000.
FOKLISTOV, an island on the E coast of Asiatic Russia, in the sea of Okhotsk, opposite the embouchure of the Ouda, to the NW of Shantarskie. It is 30 m. in length, and 6 m. in breadth.

AGRAKHAN, or AGRAGANSKI (GULF OF), an inlet of the Caspian, on the coast of Daghestan, having its opening between the mouth of the Terek on the NW and Cape Agrakhan on the SE, and extending in a SSW direction 25 m. Cape Agrakhan is in N lat. 43° 36', E long. 47° 50', 85 m. N of Derbend. A chain of islets runs out from it in a NNE direction. Of these the principal one is called Tchetchen or Chitcheena. A small river, bearing the same name as the gulf, discharges itself at its head; and on the eastern side of it, not far from the embouchure of the A., Peter the Great established a port in 1722, and erected a fort for its protection; but this establishment was destroyed in 1735.
FRANKLIN (POINT), a headland of Russian America, to the SW of Point Barrow or North cape. -Also a headland of Arctic America, in N lat. 69° 31' 13", W long. 99° 17' 58".
FRAUENBURG, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Courland, district and 40 m. W of Mittau.
FREDERICKSHAMN, a port and strong fort of Russia, in Finland, in the gov. and 54 m. WSW of Wiburg, in N lat. 60° 35'. Pop. 1,000. It was ceded to Russia in 1743.
FREDERICKSTADT, or JANUA RIGA, a small town of Russia, in the gov. of Courland, on the 1. bank of the Dwina, 48 m. E of Mitau.

FRIEDLAND, a town of Bohemia, in the circle of Bunzlau, on the Wittich, at its confluence with the Rasnitz. Pop. 3,197. It was from this place that the celebrated Wallenstein took the title of duke. It has a fine old castle, with a rich collection of ancient armour.—Also a town of East Prussia, in the circle of Konigsberg, on the l. bank of the Alle. Pop. in 1837, 2,317. It is famous for the battle gained by Bonaparte over the Russians and Prussians on the 14th of June 1807, which led to the peace of Tilsit. The loss of the allies in killed, wounded, and drowned, was nearly 20,000 men.-Also a small town of the grand duchy of Posen, on the borders of Brandenburg, 15 m. WNW of Deutsche-Krone. Pop. 2,180.—Also a small town of Moravia, 22 m. N of Olmutz. Pop. 600.- Also a town of Mecklenburg Strelitz, in the lordship of Stargard, 14 m. NE of Neu Brandenburg. Pop. 4,000.—Also a small town of Prussian Silesia, on the r. bank of the Steinau, 9 m. SSW of Waldenburg. Pop. 1,374. It has manufactures of paper and fine linen.
FROLIKHINO, a lake of Russia in Asia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, about 120 m. N of Barguzinsk, and near the E bank of Lake Baikal, into which it discharges itself.
GACHARSK, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 56 m. ENE of Mohiley, district and 13 m. NW of Mstislavl, at the confluence of the Gorodenka and Molokhva.

GADIATSCH, or GADITCH, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Poltava, 36 m. SE of Romen, at the confluence of the Khoral and the Psol, in N lat. 50° 22'. Pop. 3,641. It has an active trade in wheat, tobacco, wax, and wool, the produce of the surrounding ter-

txt: GAINA, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 24 m. N of Minsk.
GAISIN, or Hatschin, a modern town of Russia. in Europe, in the gov. of Podolia, district and 52 m. NNW of Olgopol, and 120 m. ENE of Kamenetz, on the r. bank of the Sob.
GALIOUNKA, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 98 m. ESE of Tchernigov, district and 20 m. SSW of Konotop, near the r. bank of the Romen.

GALITCH, a district and town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 69 m. NE of Kostroma, in a marshy plain, on the SE bank of a lake of the same name. The town is defended by two old forts, and contains 13 churches and a convent, and possesses several manufactories of linen. Pop. 6,000. It was founded in 1152 by the grand-duke George, surnamed Dolgorouki, and gives its name to the Galitzin family. The district is low and marshy, but pos- GAL sesses some good arable land, and considerable quantities of wood.—Lake G. is 12 m. in length, and about 5 m. in breadth.
GARINSKAIA, a town of Russia in Asia, in the gov. of Tobolsk, district and 120 m. NNW of Tournisk, on the r. bank of the Sosva.

GATTCHINA, or GATSCHINA, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 32 m. SSW of St. Petersburg, district and 14 m. SW of Sophia, on a small lake formed by the Ijorka. Pop. 8,000. It is well and regularly built, and possesses one of the finest imperial residences in Russia. It has a Greek, a Lutheran, and a Catholic church, an hospital, a foundling and a blind asylum, a horticultural school, and possesses several manufactories of hats, woollen fabrics, and porcelain. This town owes its origin to a country-seat built in the locality by Prince Gregory Orlov.
GAVRI, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Wilna, 27 m. WSW of Rossiena.
GAVRIKOVA, a port of Russia, in the gov. of Archangel, in N lat. 69° 5'.

txt: GAVRILOFSK, a village of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Tomsk, district of Barnaul, on the Tolmavaia.
GAZIMUR, a river of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, in the district of Nerchinsk, which flows into the Argun, on the l. bank, after a course of 210 m. from SW to NE.

GDOV, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 126 m. SW of St. Petersburg, on the E bank of Lake Peipus, in N lat. 58° 35'. Pop. 1,000.—Also a village of Austrian Galicia, in the circle and 15 m. WSW of Bochnia, on the Rassa.
GELENDJIK, a small bay of the Black sea, on the coast of Abassia, in N lat. 44° 35'. The Russians have a fortress here.
GELENDJIK, a small bay of the Black sea, on the coast of Abassia, in N lat. 44° 35'. The Russians have a fortress here.

GEORGENBURG, or Journberg, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Wilna, on the Niemen, 35 m. E of Tilsit. It possesses a good harbour, and is a place of considerable commerce.—Also a village of Prussia, in the reg. of Gumbinnen, N of Insterburg. Pop. 130.

GEORGIEVSK, a district and town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of the Caucasus. The district lies to the SE of that of Alexandrof and W of Mozdok. In the SW it is intersected by branches of the Caucasus chain, but towards the NE it is flat and sandy. The town is 90 m. SE of Stavrapol, and 216 GER m. NNW of Tiflis, on a lofty acclivity, near the l. bank of the Podkuma or Podkoumok. It is fortified, but is of little extent; and the houses, although built with considerable regularity, possess but little substantiality of structure. Pop., embracing that of the adjoining stanitza or military Cossack v., 3,000, chiefly Cossacks of the Volga. The governmenthouse, the churches, of which there are a Greek and an Armenian, the hospitals, the lazaretto, barracks, and public magazine of corn and salt, are the only public buildings worthy of note. The environs are pleasant, and the locality commands a magnificent view of the Caucasian mountains. This town was founded in 1771, and was formerly the cap. of the government.
GERANINI, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 44 m. S of Vilna, district and 29 m. SW of Ochmiana.
GERMANICHKI, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 44 m. S of Vilna, district and 35 m. SW of Ochmiana, near the l. bank of the Jajma.
GERMANOVKA, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 35 m. SSE of Kiev, district and 23 m. SE of Vasilkov, on the r. bank of the Krasnaia.
GETA, a small town of Russia, on the N coast of the island of Aland.
GHALGHA, a district of Circassia, on the N flank of the Caucasus, in the valley of Kumbalei.
GHIJINOSE'RO, a lake of Russia, in the gov. and 120 m. N of Olonetz. It is about 10 m. in length, and 6 m. in breadth.

GHILAN, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Astrakhan, on an island in the Volga, near the city of Astrakhan. It is chiefly inhabited by Tajiks .- Also a town of Albania, in the sanj. of Scutari, 24 m. ESE of Pristina, near the sources of the Morara. Pop. 1,300.

txt: GIZIGINSKAIA, a gulf of the Northern ocean, on the coast of Asiatic Russia, in E long. 160° 14', which receives the river Kolyma.

GJAT, or GTATSK, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Smolensk, on a river of the same name, 110 m. WSW of Moscow. Pop. 2,500. It has considerable trade in wheat, hemp, and iron.—The G. river flows NNW to the Vazouza, which it joins on the r. bank.
GLADKA (ALT and NEU), two Cossack stations in the Russian gov. of Caucasus, on the l. bank of the Terek, the former about 20 m., and the latter 30 m. above Kislar.
GLADKA (ALT and NEU), two Cossack stations in the Russian gov. of Caucasus, on the l. bank of the Terek, the former about 20 m., and the latter 30 m. above Kislar.
GLASOV, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Viatka, on the l. bank of the Tcheptsa, 100 m. E by S of Viatka.
GLIGVI, a town of Daghestan, 90 m. N of Tiflis.
GLINSK, a small town of Russia, in the gov. of Pultava, 80 m. SE of Czernigov, on the r. bank of the Soula.
GLINTISHKI, a town of Russia, in the ov. and 21 m. N of Vilna.

GLU'CHOV, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Czernigov, pleasantly situated on the Yesman river, 40 m. ESE of Novgorod-Sieverskoi. Its streets are regular; and it contains 7 or 8 churches, and 2 convents. Pop. 8,000. Clay of a particular quality is found in the neighbourhood, and sent to the porcelain manufactories of Moscow and St. Petersburg. A large proportion of the coarse woollens employed in clothing the Russian army is manufactured here. G. was nearly consumed by fire in 1782.
GLUCKTHAL, a district of Russia, in the gov. of Cherson, near Tiraspol, colonised by German emigrants.
GLUSK, or GLOUSK, a small town of Russia, in 345. the gov. of Minsk, on the r. bank of the Plitch, 48 m. E by S of Sloutsk.—Also a small town of Poland, 4 m. S of Lublin.
GNEZNO, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 48 m. SSE of Grodno.

GNILOOSKOI, a fortress of Russia, in the gov. of Astrakhan, on the r. bank of the Oural, 14 m. NE of Ouralsk.—Also a town of Russia, in the Don Cossack territory, 15 m. NE of Azof, on the r. bank of the Mertvoi-Donetz, a branch of the Don.

GNILOOSKOI, a fortress of Russia, in the gov. of Astrakhan, on the r. bank of the Oural, 14 m. NE of Ouralsk.—Also a town of Russia, in the Don Cossack territory, 15 m. NE of Azof, on the r. bank of the Mertvoi-Donetz, a branch of the Don.
GNILUSHKA, a German colony in the Russian gov. of Saratof, district of Kamishin, on a small stream of the same name, an affluent of the Havla. Pop. 300.
GOBZA, a river of Russia, in the gov. of Smolensk, rising near Efremovo, running W, and joining the Kasplia on the r. bank, after a course of 36 m.
GOGOLEV, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Chernigov, 27 m. SSE of Oster.
GOJA, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 16 m. NNE of Grodno, near the r. bank of the Niemen.

GOKSHAI, a river of Asiatic Russia, in the khanate of Shirvan, rising in the Baba-dagh, a principal summit of the E. Caucasus, and flowing S to the Kur. GOKSHAI (LAKE), SEVAN, OF GOKTSCHE-DENGIS, a large lake of Georgia, in the circle of Erivan, between the parallels of 40° 8' and 40° 40', and intersected by the meridian of 45° E. It stretches 40 m. in a NNW and SSE direction; and varies in breadth from 10 to 24 m. The country slopes on all sides to the lake.
GOLAYA, a mountain-ridge in the SE of the Crimea, connected with the Tokluk-Syrt.
GOLDINGEN, or KULDIGA, a small town of Russia, in the gov. of Courland, on the l. bank of the Windau, 60 m. W by N of Mittau. It is irregularly built, and covers a large extent of ground.
GOLDOV, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 54
GOLIH, a town of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Irkutzk, on the Lena.
GOLINKA, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 36 m. S of Grodno, on the r. bank of the Svislotch.— Also another town in the same gov. 63 m. SE of Grodno.
GOLINKA, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 36 m. S of Grodno, on the r. bank of the Svislotch.— Also another town in the same gov. 63 m. SE of Grodno.
GOLLIAVINA, a village of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Tobolsk, 188 m. E of Yenisei.
GOLOLOBOFKA, a German colony in the Russian gov. of Saratof, on a small affluent of the Kamichin. It consisted in 1812 of 105 Lutheran families.
GOLOVANEVSK, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Podolia, 52 m. NE of Balta. Pop. 500.
GOLOVNINO, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 27 m. WNW of Mohilev.
GOLTA, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Cherson, on the r. bank of the Bug, opposite the confluence of the Sinioukha.
GOLTVA, a town of Russia, the chief place of a district, 60 m. SW of Poltava.
GOLUBINSKAIA, a town of Russia, in the territory of the Don-Cossacks, on the r. bank of the Don, 210 m. NE of Novo-Cherkask.
GOLUSTNA, a village of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. and 40 m. ESE of Irkutsk, on the l. bank of the Biukal lake.
GOMEL, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 105 m. SSE of Mohiley, on the r. bank of the Soj.

GOMRI-SHAI, a river of Daghestan, in the khanate of Kaitach, rising in the mountains of Dargo, and flowing E, and NE to Kjajakent, where it discharges itself into the Caspian, 5 m. NNW of the Gadshi lake.

GORBATOF, a town of European Russia, in the gov. of Nizni-Novgorod, on the Oker, a little below the confluence of the Kliasma, 41 m. SW of Nizni- Novgorod. Pop. 2,070. The surrounding country is fertile in grain, lint, and hemp.

GORBITZKOI, a fort of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, at the confluence of the Chilka and the Little Gorbitza. GORCAH, GORCHA, or GORKHA, a rajaship or district of Nepal, situated between the 28th and 29th parallels, in the fork between the Marichangdi and Trisulganga. It is a mountainous barren country, intersected by numerous hill streams.-Its capital, of the same name, is situated on the summit of a lofty hill, in N lat. 27° 52', E long. 84° 22'. Pop. 10,000. After the conquest of Nepal in 1768, the seat of government was transferred to Catmandu, and the city of G. has fallen into comparative decay
GORDJDI, or GARSDEN, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Wilna, 36 m. WSW of Telsh, on the r. bank of the Minge.
GORDOM, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 165 m. NW of Wilna, on the Tenne.

GORI, a town of Russian Georgia, in the district of Kartli, on the Kur, 43 m. NW of Tiflis. Pop. 3,000. It is defended by a fortress on the l. bank of the Didi-Liakhei, which here joins the Kur.—Also a town of Russia, in the gov. and 45 m. NE of Mohilev.
GORK-SOLENOE, a lake of Russia, in the gov. of Saratof, 60 m. SE of Kamoitchen. It is 12 m. in length from SSE to NNW, and about 5 m. in greatest breadth.
GORNOSTAIPOL, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 43 m. NNW of Kiev, on the l. bank of the Teterev. Pop. 500.

GOROBLAGODAT, a town of Russia, in the gov. of Perm, N of Tagilsk. There are large iron-mines in the vicinity, in the Blagodat, a rich magnetic mountain, which rises about 450 ft. above the plain of the Kushva.
GORODETZ, a small town of Russia, in the gov. of Grodno, 10 m. E of Kobrin.
GORODILOVO, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 66 m. ESE of Vilna.
GORODIN, a town of Russia, in the gov. and 92 m. W of Poltava, on the l. bank of the Soula.

IRTISH, a river of Asia, which has its source in Sungaria, towards the SE extremity of the Great Altaï mountains, in N lat. 46° 45'. It runs first WNW through a wide valley enclosed on the ENE by the Great Altaï, and on the S by the Altaï-Alintopa; issues thence on the W through Lake Taisan, or Kong-ko-lu, in the Chinese territory, and flowing N to the confluence of the Narim, enters Asiatic Russia; traverses, with great velocity, in a WNW direction, the steppes in the E part of the prov. of Omsk; thence bends its course, first N, then WNW, into the gov. of Tobolsk, till it reaches the town of that name, when it again curves N, and, after considerable sinuosities, reaches the Obi, which it joins, having run after a longer course than the Obi itself, on the l. bank, a little above Samarovo, and 150 m. W of Surgut, in N lat. 60° 45'. It has a total course of about 1,950 m., of which 720 m. are within the Chinese empire, 750 m. in the prov. of Omsk, and 480 m. in the gov. of Tobolsk. At its point of junction with the Obi, it has a width of 13 verst, and a depth of 50 ft.; while the Obi has a width of 10 versts, and is 300 ft. deep. Its principal affluents are in the Chinese empire, on the r., the Boroi, Kaba, Kurtchum, and Narim; in the prov. of Omsk, the Bukhtarma, Ulba, Uba, and Om, on the r., and the Tchar-Gurban, Tchaganka, Tunduk, and Kamishlovka, on the I.; and in the gov. …

GRODNO, an extensive province or government of Russia, forming part of Lithuania, and bounded by the gov. of Vilna on the N; by Minsk on the E; by Volhynia on the S; and Bialystock and Poland on the W. Its superficial extent is 14,705 sq. m. The surface, which belongs to the basins of the Niemen on the N, the Dnieper on the SE, and the Vistula on the SW, is generally level, and much of it, especially in the NE, is still covered with wood; a light sandy soil, partly marshy, but in general fertile, occurs in other quarters, and in the S are some very extensive marshes. The Bog, with its affluents the Lesna and the Moukhavetz, and the Narev, with its affluents the Kolorona and the Narevka, water this gov.; and on the SE it is intersected by the Jasiolda. Agriculture is here in a backward state, yet corn is exported, besides flour, flax, hemp, wool, hops, wax, honey, wood, and potash; and the number of cattle reared is large. There are some manufactories of woollen cloth, leather, and paper; and the little trade that is carried on is in the hands of the Jews. This country is divided into 8 circles: viz., G., Lida, Novogrodek, Slonim, Volkovüsk, Prujany, Kobrin, and Brest-Litowsky. Pop. in 1839, 536,403, of whom 73,470 were Jews, and about 1,000 Tartars. The nobility are principally Poles. In 1835, there were 32 public schools, attended by 1,485 scholars, within this gov.

It consists of a few scattered cabins, and has a castle belonging to the duke of Richelieu. This village was known to the Greeks under the name of Eristhena. On the side of one of the adjacent mountains are the ruins of a fort and of a church; and in the midst of these stand several columns supposed to have been brought from the Parthenon of Athens. There are also some remains of a wall running along the edge of rocky precipices, down which the tyrant of the Taurida threw his captives.

txt: SWEABORG, or SVEABORG, an important Russian fortress, in the gulf of Finland, 3 m. SE of Helsingfors, from the quays of which, says Dr. Milner, its granite ramparts may be seen, with the roofs of the buildings it contains, consisting of barracks, magazines, prisons, and a limited number of private houses. It completely commands the seaward passage to the city, or the narrow Gustaf-sound, the only channel which has water deep enough for large vessels. The fortifications extend over six islands, or rather rocks, Langörn, Lilla-Swartö, Vester- Swartö, Oster Swartö, Vargön, and Gustafsvärd. The last five are connected by bridges, and occupy a space of about 1,200 by 650 yds. Vargon is considered the citadel, and is somewhat central. The only practicable passage between the islands lies between Treksholm and Gustafsvard. All these islands bristle with cannon, and are grim with ramparts. The works, which are of granite, and are as massive as the foundations upon which they are built, being for the most part constructions out of the solid rock, are said to mount 810 cannon, to have casemates for from 6,000 to 7,000 small arms, and barrack-room for a garrison of 12,000 men. Count Ehrenswerd, field-marshal of Sweden, superintended the construction of the first fortress, the citadel of Vargön, begun in 1747 and finished in 1758, during the reign of Adolphus Frederic. HAPSAL, HABSAL, or GAPSAL, a district and town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Esthonia. bay of the Baltic, to the S of the island of Nouko, to the E of that of Dago, and 60 m. SW of Revel, in N lat. 58° 54'. Pop. 1,500. It has a Lutheran church, and 2 schools. Large markets are held here twice a-year. The port is annually frequented by numerous vessels, which carry on an active import trade in salt, wine, spices, and other commodities, and export large quantities of corn, lint, wax, and juniper berries. This town was built in 1279, by Bishop Herman. It was taken by the Danes in 1559, and in 1645 by the Swedes, by whom it was retained till 1710, when it fell into the hands of the Russians. It was formerly the seat of the bishop of Œsel, and contained a fine cathedral, the ruins of which still exist.—The district comprises the ancient territory of Wieck or Vick, and forms the most westerly part of Esthonia. It produces grain, lint, and in small quantities hops. Cattle are reared in great numbers on its pastures, and the coasts abound with fish. Pop. 41,000. …

ICHIM, or Ishim, a river of Russia in Asia, which has its source in a mountainous district near the central part of the gov. of Omsk, in N lat. 50° 35', and E long. 74°. It runs first WNW, then makes a considerable circuit, and pursuing its course in a NNE direction into the gov. of Tobolsk, joins the Irtish on the l. bank, 130 m. ESE of Tobolsk, and after a total course of 1,200 m. Its principal affluents are the Kaluton, Akbasar, Kulai-Agir-Barluk, and Nova Barluk on the r.; and on the l. the Nura, which conveys to it the waters of Lake Kurgaldjin, and forms the principal head-stream of the I. and the Terschan. Alexandrovskaia, Petropavlosk, and Ichim are the only towns of importance on its banks. In the lower part of its course it is skirted by several villages and numerous ancient tombs. This river flows in nearly its entire extent through the vast plain named the steppe of Ichim. This plain is studded with numerous lakes, but presents complete sterility. A line of military posts, bearing the name of Ichim, extends along the S part of the gov. of Omsk, from fort Stanovoi to the fortress of Omsk, at the confluence of the Om and Irtish, erected in the reign of the Empress Anne for the defence of the gov. of Tobolsk from the incursions of the Kirghiz.—Also a town, capital of a district in the gov. and 170 m. ILGA, a river of Russia in Asia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, which issues from a small lake, 90 m. NNE of Irkutsk, runs N, passes Ilginsk, and joins the Lena at Usk-Ilghinskaïa, after a total course of about 150 m.
ILIMSK, a town of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, 260 m. N of Irkutsk, on the r. bank of the Ilim. Pop. 700, chiefly employed in hunting martins and sables in the adjacent forests.
ILINKA, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 84 m. SSW of Voronej, district and 30 m. SW of Ostrogojsk.
ILINTZKOI, a town of Russia in Asia, in the gov. and 132 m. E of Irkutsk, district and 36 m. NW of Verkhne-Oudinsk, on the l. bank of the Selinga, and E of Lake Baikal.

ILLORI, or ILORI, a fort of Russia in Asia, in Abkasia, in the principality of Mingrelia, 33 m. SE of Sukgum-kaleh, on the l. bank of the Caladsva. To the W of this fort, on the shore of the Black sea, are the ruins of the ancient town of the same name.

ILLORI, or ILORI, a fort of Russia in Asia, in Abkasia, in the principality of Mingrelia, 33 m. SE of Sukgum-kaleh, on the l. bank of the Caladsva. To the W of this fort, on the shore of the Black sea, are the ruins of the ancient town of the same name.

ILLOUKST, or ILLUXT, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Courland, district and 51 m. SSE of Alt-Zelburg, and 81 m. ESE of Mitau. It contains a fine castle and 3 churches-a Catholic, a Greek, and a Protestant.

ILIDJA-VARNA, a town of Turkey, in Bulgaria, on the Black sea, 9 m. S of Varna. ILIJEH [i. e., 'warm spring'], a village of Asiatic Turkey, 6 m. W of Erzerum, and 3 m. E of the Euphrates, which is here 60 or 70 yds. wide in summer. It has 2 warm springs of a temp. of 100°.— Also a town of Asiatic Turkey, in the pash. and 72 m. WNW of Diarbekir, on the l. bank of the Euphrates.—Also a village of Asiatic Turkey, in the pash. and 60 m. ENE of Diarbekir, at an alt. of 3,779 ft. above sea-level. It contains 4 fountains and 2 mosques. ILIM, a river of Asiatic Russia, in the gov. of Irkutsk, which rises in the SW part of the district of Kerensk; and running N, and then NW, joins the Angara on the r. bank, after a course of 210 m. ILIMANI, NEVADO-DE-ILLIMANI, or YLLIMANI, a majestic summit of the Andes, second to that of Sorata, in the Bolivian prov. of La Paz, 30 m. ESE of the town of that name. Like Chimborazo in the Andes of Quito, I. is the most southern snowy summit of the eastern branch of the Andes, to which it belongs. By astronomical observation it is fixed between 16° 35' and 16° 39' S lat., and 67° and 68° W long. It has three peaks, arranged pretty nearly ILI from N to S. Mr. Pentland, in 1827, measured the most northerly of these peaks, and found its elevation to be 24,200 ft. above the level of the sea, or nearly 12,000 ft. …

txt: ILMEN, a lake of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and district and to the S of Novgorod. It is of triangular form, and has a superficies 35 m. in length from E to W, and 27 m. at its greatest breadth. It receives the Msta on the N, the Lovat on the S, and the Cheson on the W, and discharges itself by the branch of industry is the working of minerals, and | Volkhof, which flows N to Lake Ladoga. Frequent tempests occur on this lake, and render its navigation dangerous. Vessels pass direct from the Msta to the Volkhof by the canal of Novogorodsky.

ILMA, or ILMUS, the river ILM in Germany. ILMA, ILM or ILMSTADT in Germany. ICIUM PROMONTORIUM, CAPE GRIS-NEZ in the | ILMENAVIA, ILMENAU in Saxe-Weimar. ILMENUS LACUS, LAKE ILMEN in the Russian gov. of Novgorod.

ILMOLA, a town and parish of Russia in Europe, in the grand duchy of Finland, gov. and 39 m. SE of Vasa, and 54 m. NE of Christinestad, and district of Soedra-Korsholms. The environs produce excellent rye.
ILOKI, a town of Russia in Europe, in the gov. and 192 m. NW of Vilna, district and 30 m. NNW of Teleh.
ILOMANTS, a town and parish of Russia in Europe, in the grand duchy of Finland, gov. and 87 m. ESE of Kuopio, and 90 m. NE of Nyslots. The chase forms the chief employment of the inhabitants.
ILOVLINSKAIA, a town of Russia, in the territory of the Don Cossacks, on the l. bank of the Ilovla, a little above the confluence of that river with the Don.

hier: gov. of Saratov > district of Kamichin > gov. of the Don Cossacks
txt: ILOVLA, a river of Russia in Europe, which has its source in the gov. of Saratov, and district of Kamichin, to the N of Kamenka, and 9 m. W of the r. bank of the Volga; flows in a SSW direction into the gov. of the Don Cossacks; and unites with the Don, on the r. bank, a little above Ilovlinskaïa, and after a total course of 210 m. Several German colonies have been established on its banks. A canal was projected in the reign of Catherine II., for the purpose of connecting the Don and the Volga by means of this river and the Kamichinka; but was abandoned, in consequence of the level of the Don at the junction of the I. being found to be 106 yds. above that of the Volga.

GVOSDIVI, or GWOSDEFF, a group of small islands in Behring's straits, between the E extremity of Siberia and Russian America, in N lat. 65° 40', W long. 173° 50'. They are 4 in number, and are named Ousken, Igheplin, Imaglin, and Ratmanof. The three first were discovered in 1775, by Kovalev, and the last by Kotzebue. They are low, and possess little vegetation. Their inhabitants are Tshuktshes, and subsist on the flesh of the reindeer, and on fish. Imaglin, which is the largest island in the group, is 30 m. in length, about 3 m. in breadth, and contains a pop. of about 400.

IMIRITIA, a principality of Asiatic Russia, situated in the Western Caucasian regions, and bounded on the N by the principal chain of Caucasus; on the E by Georgia; on the S by Akhalzike; and on the W by Guriel and Mingrelia. It is watered by the Rioni, and numerous tributary streams, the course of most of which is interrupted by cataracts. The Tzchenesstzquali separates it from Mingrelia. The climate is extremely mild; snow seldom lies on the ground, and the rivers are never frozen over. Much of the surface consists of rocks and mountains, interspersed with fertile valleys and plains. Abundance of fruit of the finest flavour grows wild, and the trunk of the vine is here known to attain 15 inches in diam. Entire hills are overgrown with olive, myrtle, laurel, chestnut, and valuable timber trees; and the lower grounds present almond, fig, quince, pear, and plum trees, the latter sometimes bearing twice a-year. Copious harvests of grain, also of cotton, hemp, and flax, are obtained. The pop. of the principality is computed at 20,000 families, whose personal appearance is superior to that of their neighbours, but they are in general an indolent, distrustful, and proud race, though distinguished by the virtue of hospitality. As nearly the whole inhabitants dwell in solitary hamlets, the country contains scarcely any towns except Cotatis or Kutais, the capital, situated on the r. …

IMZA, a river of Russia in Europe, in the gov. of Nijnei-Novgorod, which has its source in the district of Knaiginin; passes the town of that name; pursues its course to the E; and, after running a total distance of 45 m., joins the Ourga.
INBATSKOI, a village of Russia in Asia, in the gov. and district and 375 m. NNW of Yenisei, on the r. bank of the river of that name, 57 m. SE of the v. of Nijne-Inbatskaïa.
